definitions.explanation: Describes someone whose conduct and manners are proper and refined.

examples.japanese: ⟦{行儀|ぎょうぎ}→行儀：02662_gyougi⟧⟦よく→よく：00601_yoku⟧⟦{座|すわ}り→座る：00757_suwaru⟧⟦なさい→なさる：01307_nasaru⟧。
{食事中|しょくじちゅう}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{行儀|ぎょうぎ}→行儀：02662_gyougi⟧⟦よく→よく：00601_yoku⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧よう⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{親|おや}→親：01357_oya⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{言|い}われて→言う：00515_iu⟧⟦{育|そだ}った→育つ：01951_sodatsu⟧。
examples.english: I was raised being told by my parents to behave properly during meals.

notes:
⟦{行儀|ぎょうぎ}→行儀：02662_gyougi⟧ means manners or conduct, particularly at the table or in social situations. The full expression {行儀|ぎょうぎ}が{良|よ}い describes someone whose behavior meets social standards. Often used about children. The adverbial form ⟦{行儀|ぎょうぎ}→行儀：02662_gyougi⟧⟦よく→よく：00601_yoku⟧ (properly, with good manners) is very common.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{行儀|ぎょうぎ}→行儀：02662_gyougi⟧⟦よく→よく：00601_yoku⟧⟦{食|た}べる→食べる：00396_taberu⟧: to eat with good manners
- ⟦{行儀|ぎょうぎ}→行儀：02662_gyougi⟧⟦よく→よく：00601_yoku⟧⟦{座|すわ}る→座る：00757_suwaru⟧: to sit properly
- ⟦{行儀|ぎょうぎ}→行儀：02662_gyougi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{悪|わる}い→悪い：00908_warui⟧: ill-mannered, badly behaved
- お⟦{行儀|ぎょうぎ}→行儀：02662_gyougi⟧: manners (with polite prefix, often used with children)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{礼儀正|れいぎただ}しい→礼儀正しい：15088_reigitadashii⟧: polite, courteous — focuses on formal politeness and social etiquette
- ⟦{品|ひん}→品：03712_hin⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦いい→いい：00118_ii⟧: elegant, refined — emphasizes class and sophistication
- ⟦{躾|しつけ}→躾：10342_shitsuke⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦いい→いい：00118_ii⟧: well-disciplined — focuses on upbringing and training
- ⟦マナー→マナー：11139_manaa⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦いい→いい：00118_ii⟧: to have good manners — loanword equivalent, often used in public/social contexts
